beliefs.practice: Read the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string only from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit it to source; use a .env.example placeholder and fetch secrets from a secret store (Azure Key Vault) in production.

Configure the MongoDB driver connection pool and timeouts explicitly (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) and set an appName in the URI so connection behavior is predictable and diagnosable.
Enable TLS/SSL and verify server certificates when connecting (mongodb+srv or mongodb:// with tls=true); reject insecure (tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true) settings in production.

Do not embed large binary blobs or very large strings inline; store original response text and embeddings as separate fields with size limits documented (e.g., embeddings as fixed-length float arrays) and avoid documents bigger than the DB's max document size.

Model enrichment outputs as typed fields: original_text (string), themes (array[string]), sentiment (enum string), representative_quote (string), embedding (array[float] with fixed dimension), and store metadata (source_id, question_id, created_at).

Create standard (non-vector) indexes for fields used in aggregations and filters: question_id, themes (as multikey index), sentiment, created_at; use compound indexes for the most frequent aggregation patterns (e.g., {question_id:1, 'themes':1}).

For vector search, create a dedicated vector index on the embedding field with explicit algorithm and parameters (dimension, metric: cosine or innerProduct, and algorithm options such as M/efConstruction for HNSW or IVF parameters) rather than relying on default B-tree indexing.

Keep a documented, fixed embedding dimension per deployment (e.g., 1536 for common OpenAI models); validate embedding length on write and reject mismatched vectors before inserting into the collection.

When running aggregation pipelines to compute top themes and sentiment distribution: project only needed fields, $unwind the themes array, $group by theme or sentiment, $sort and $limit; use $facet to compute multiple aggregates in one pipeline to reduce RU consumption.
Use server-side aggregation rather than fetching all documents client-side for analytics; rely on indexed filters (question_id) before heavy pipeline stages to minimize scanned documents.

Enable and rely on driver-provided retryable reads and retryable writes when possible (retryReads/retryWrites), and implement exponential backoff with jitter for higher-level retry logic around idempotent enrichment or seeding operations.

Write enrichment outputs idempotently: include a unique enrichment_run_id or use upsert with a deterministic key (e.g., document_id + enrichment_version) so repeated runs or retries do not create duplicates or inconsistent state.

Avoid multi-document transactions for high-throughput pipelines; design documents to be self-contained (single-document updates) where possible. If transactions are required, keep them short and use the driver transaction API.

Limit the size of arrays that are frequently unwound (e.g., themes): cap the number of stored theme tags per document, or store theme counts in a separate aggregation/summary collection to speed analytic queries.

When embedding third-party LLM/embedding providers, treat the external call as a separate bounded step: persist the original text, then call the model; on success, atomically update the document (or use an upsert) and log the model version, prompts, and embedding model name for reproducibility and debugging.

Restrict network access to the DocumentDB cluster via firewall rules or VNet integration; do not leave the cluster open to the public internet without IP or VNet restrictions, and log/admin alert on new IPs being allowed.

If the platform supports it, create vector indexes via the server's index API with the exact index definition recorded in code or IaC; when automated index creation fails, include the index JSON in README so operators can create it manually (document expected fields: field name, dimension, metric, algorithm options).

Measure and monitor RU or I/O cost of aggregation and vector queries; add query sampling and slow-query logging and tune indexes based on explain plans. Use the provider's explain tool (MCP or explain()) to validate index usage.
Avoid storing raw LLM prompts with PII in-line; redact or encrypt sensitive content before persisting, or store only non-sensitive metadata and hashes for traceability.

Seed scripts should be idempotent and limited in scope (e.g., load example documents into the sample_customer_360_17 database only), and should validate the target DB name from the environment to avoid accidental writes to other databases.

Use ODM patterns appropriately: when using Beanie, initialize Beanie with models and an AsyncIOMotorClient; perform bulk writes with bulk_write/upsert where supported and avoid per-document synchronous blocking calls.
For vector nearest-neighbor queries, limit candidate set via metadata filters (e.g., question_id) before invoking the vector index to reduce cost and improve latency.
Document and track the index schema in version control (index JSON or create_index commands) and keep migration scripts or manual operator steps that can recreate indexes if automated creation fails.
Protect against schema drift in production: validate documents at ingest/enrichment time (embedding length, theme types, sentiment enum) and emit metrics on rejected/invalid documents.
